description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Having become brahman, serene in self, one neither grieves nor desires and is the same toward all beings; one then attains supreme devotion (18.54).

description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Asked whether his delusion born of ignorance is destroyed (18.72), Arjuna reports: delusion destroyed, memory (smṛti) regained by Kṛṣṇa's grace, standing firm with doubt gone, ready to do his word (18.73).

description: Sañjaya calls the dialogue wondrous and hair-raising (romaharṣaṇa) (18.74); recalling it again and again he rejoices again and again (18.76); recalling Hari's most wondrous form, great is his amazement (vismaya) and he rejoices again and again (18.77).

description: Bhagavad Gītā 16–18: Sāttvic happiness is delighted in through practice, ends sorrow, is like poison at first and nectar in the end, and is born of the clarity (prasāda) of ātma-buddhi, one's own understanding or the understanding of the self; rājasic happiness, from sense-contact, is nectar at first and poison in the end; tāmasic happiness deludes one's self first and last and arises from sleep, sloth and heedlessness (18.36–39).
